newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta share index plunges on Sampoerna losses.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta share index plunges on Sampoerna losses.

text.p: Jakarta's stock index plunged almost two percent on Tuesday as a steep fall in cigarette maker PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna triggered wide selling of blue-chips, brokers said.

Sampoerna, which has been hit by a series of negative reports since it bought a stake in automobile manufacturer Astra International, dived 11.36 percent to 18,725 rupiah ($8.14), as the composite index fell 1.97 percent to 574.78 points.

"There is certainly a spillover effect from Sampoerna on to the market today as foreign investors are really concerned about what is going to happen in Sampoerna," Jason McCay, an analyst with Peregrine Sewu Securities, told Reuters.

He said the negative reports about Sampoerna were making foreign investors wary of Indonesian stocks in general. "I think generally this is a doubtful example of how to invest shareholder funds," he added.
Sampoerna has been criticised for investing in Astra, and ratings agencies Moody's and Standard & Poor's have put its long-term debt on review.
Sampoerna said last month that a wholly-owned subsidiary had bought a 2.85 percent stake in Astra at the peak of a wave of buying into Indonesia's largest car manufacturer.
Separately, Sampoerna's majority shareholder and founder, Putera Sampoerna, announced he had bought a 9.81 stake in Astra on his individual account.

Putera Sampoerna now effectively controls the largest stake in Astra but has not said what his immediate plans are. PT Sampoerna is scheduled to hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on November 2.

Brokers said they were also concerned that Sampoerna had secured a fresh $400-million stand-by loan last week on top of $200 million in notes issued by subsidiary Sampoerna International Finance Co B.V. in June.

Moody's said on Monday the moves "clearly indicate that Sampoerna intends to pursue a much more aggressive diversification strategy away from its original plan as well as its willingness to use a higher level of debt capacity for this purpose".

Moody's said its review would focus on the prospects for further investment by Sampoerna in Astra and, if the investment materialised, the method of financing, its impact on the predictability of the company's overall cash flow and the magnitude of additional business and political risk incurred.

"While the magnitude of the investment is not at this point material, Standard & Poor's considers this investment to be outside the expected expansion parameters of Sampoerna and could lead to heightened credit risk," S & P said last week.
McCay of Peregrine said he changed his recommendation on Sampoerna from "buy" to "hold" when the company announced its purchase in Astra.
"Our recommendation at this point is a hold until we get further explanations from the company on what they are going to do in the near future," he said.

Brokers said the fall in the Jakarta index was also due to some foreign-led profit-taking of other selected heavyweights such as conglomerate Bimantara Citra and toll-road operator Citra Marga and was in line with a drop on Wall Street overnight.
"Technically it's normal for some blue-chips to consolidate as they had risen sharply recently. But today's sharp fall is trigerred by Sampoerna," said an analyst from a Singapore-based company.
